I was experimenting with using these 2 Parallel Map Event Pages to map the "i" key to open the background for an Inventory menu.

If I map a bunch of keys this way at the beginning of my game, will they persist? Meaning I will always be able to run a parallel event to see if they are being triggered?
Or is this specific to the map that the Event is on? Or is this only until the game is reloaded like after a save? Or is there some other limitation?

Second question. Assuming the above method of mapping keys persists in the game, are there any problems with doing this? Or having a Parallel Event running to constantly check for those keys to be triggered and then do something? Like call Common Events.
Thanks for any clarification that you can provide!

posts.author: caethyril
posts.body:
By default the input maps are initialised on game boot, then remain unchanged. So as you've seen, any changes made will persist for the rest of the play session, i.e. until you close the game.
Like ShadowDragon said, to make this into a plugin, you can simply put the code you have into its own
.js
file. That way, it'll apply itself when the game boots up. E.g.
JavaScript:
/*:
 * @target MZ
 * @plugindesc Add custom keyboard controls.
 * @url https://forums.rpgmakerweb.com/threads/174276/
 * @help Free to use and/or modify for any project, no credit required.
 */
Input.keyMapper[73] = 'i';
The header is optional, mostly for display purposes.
@target MZ
suppresses the "may not be written for MZ" warning in the Plugin Manager, which can be helpful to avoid hiding legitimate warnings from other plugins.

I don't imagine there would be any problems based purely on quantity, no. Just be aware which buttons already have an assigned response:
Spoiler:
core keymapper
JavaScript:
Input.keyMapper = {
    9: "tab", // tab
    13: "ok", // enter
    16: "shift", // shift
    17: "control", // control
    18: "control", // alt
    27: "escape", // escape
    32: "ok", // space
    33: "pageup", // pageup
    34: "pagedown", // pagedown
    37: "left", // left arrow
    38: "up", // up arrow
    39: "right", // right arrow
    40: "down", // down arrow
    45: "escape", // insert
    81: "pageup", // Q
    87: "pagedown", // W
    88: "escape", // X
    90: "ok", // Z
    96: "escape", // numpad 0
    98: "down", // numpad 2
    100: "left", // numpad 4
    102: "right", // numpad 6
    104: "up", // numpad 8
    120: "debug" // F9
};
A button can't have two names assigned to it, e.g.
Input.keyMapper[90] = "z";
would prevent the Z key from acting in its usual role as an alternative "ok" input.
(Also, remember that the
keyMapper
is only for keyboard input, not gamepad or touch.)
ZombieKidzRule said:
Or maybe you would need to have multiple Parallel Events running to check them all without experiencing any sort of delay or performance impact?
Click to expand...
No, use 1 Parallel event for all the checks! RPG Maker processes its events in series: having multiple Parallels for the "same thing" like you describe is a waste of memory.

posts.author: caethyril
posts.body:
ZombieKidzRule said:
I am getting ready to test it now and see if it also recognizes the letter if the CAPS lock is on or if the SHIFT key is also being pressed for a capital letter.
Click to expand...
No: shift & capslock are their own keys. E.g. the core mapper assigns the shift key (code
16
) to the name
"shift"
. That's the internal name for the dash button.
Each key on the keyboard has a unique code. This is the code by which the
keyMapper
is indexed. When a key is pressed (e.g.
Z
), the game checks its
keyMapper
for the code of that key (
90
). If present, it then flags the associated "button name" (
"ok"
) as being in a "pressed" state.
The rest of the engine uses these "button name states" to decide how to respond to user input. So if a key is pressed but its code isn't listed in the mapper, the game will effectively ignore it.
Also, just a note for the plugin header: you can use
@author
to specify who made it, e.g.
JavaScript:
/*:
* @target MZ
* @plugindesc Add custom keyboard controls.
* @author ZombieKidzRule (with help from caethyril)
* @url https://forums.rpgmakerweb.com/threads/174276
* @Help Free to use and/or modify for any project, no credit required.
*/
Again, it's just display info, you can keep it in the help section if you prefer~
Norintha said:
should it not be saving that info?
Click to expand...
Well. The core scripts shouldn't, because they have no code for it. But key-mapping plugins certainly should, otherwise you'd have to reconfigure the controls every time you launch the game!

Click to expand...
To be sure, you could try turning off all plugins, save your project to apply Plugin Manager changes, then test. That should prevent it from happening. You could then turn plugins back on, one by one or in small groups, to try to narrow down the culprit. (Or just ignore it, if it's not causing problems.)

ZombieKidzRule said:
If anyone knows an easier, more efficient way to achieve the same results I would be very happy to learn how to do it!
Click to expand...
Whenever I am using a parallel event/common event, I try to avoid any other types of loops unless I have to. For the most part, how your event is set up would work great for a single script call.
If I am using a bit more lines than usual in a script call, I rewrite it as a function (plugin) and call the function instead to help with performance, troubleshooting, debugging, and reading.
Feel free to use it and modify as you see fit.
Video:
Spoiler
Code:
Spoiler
JavaScript:
/* zombiePicture Notes:
    - Declare variables:
        str: string of input keys
        arr: picture X coordinates
        key: previous button triggered
        ix1:  index for string/array
        ix2: index for pictures
        scr:  reference to $gameScreen
        pic:  create an array for the first 5 entries
                of $gameScreen._pictures; filter out
                any empty (null/undefined) entries
    - Check if the player's input matches string in str
    - If picture ix2 (index) is present, delete it
    - If the length of the array of pictures is less than 1,
        show the specific picture
    - This prevents other pictures being shown (only 1 can
        be shown at a time and must be removed before any
        other pictures in that range can be shown)
    - Console log for testing only - please remove when ready
        to avoid performance hit with console.
*/
function zombiePicture() {
    const str = 'fprc',
          arr = [5, 170, 335, 500],
          key = Input._latestButton,
          ix1 = str.indexOf(key),
          ix2 = ix1 + 1,
          scr = $gameScreen,
          pic = scr._pictures.slice(0, 5).filter(x => x);
    if (Input.isTriggered(str[ix1])) {
        if (scr.picture(ix2)) {
            scr.erasePicture(ix2);
        }
        if (pic.length < 1) {
            scr.showPicture(ix2, `D${ix2}`, 0, arr[ix1], 0, 100, 100, 255, 0);
        }
        console.log(`Key: ${str[ix1]}, Picture: ${ix2} - ${!!scr.picture(ix2)}`);
    }
};
Photos:
Spoiler
I did not use a wait frame here because the timing is very important since it depends upon user input (a 1 wait frame caused some delay issues that didn't really pick up the key input properly) - if you want to use a higher frame wait, I would recommend changing Input.isTriggered() to Input.isPressed() with a wait frame of at least 6 frames.
Also, when key inputs are important on every frame, I usually defer it to an eventlistener instead and go from there. It is a bit more complicated to set up, though. I believe Poryg had a good tutorial on something like it.
In your case, you would rename `D${ix2}` to simply `${ix2}` since your pictures are named 1, 2, 3, and 4. Hope this helps!
